subject: chemistry
title: Bonding & Structure: Properties Decoded
welcome_lead: Now connect structure to behaviour: why diamond is hard, why metals bend, why salt melts then conducts.
meta_desc: GCSE Chemistry — explaining hardness, conductivity and malleability from structure.
final_note: You can explain hardness, conductivity and malleability directly from bonding and structure.

concepts.def: Electron free to move through a structure
Shared pair of electrons between atoms
Can be hammered into shape without shattering

walkthroughs.h2: Why diamond is hard and graphite isn't
walkthroughs.body_html:
Same element, different bonding pattern → very different properties.

Diamond: every carbon is bonded to 4 others by strong covalent bonds. A 3D rigid network — super hard, very high melting point, no free electrons → poor conductor.

Graphite: each carbon bonds to 3 others in hexagonal layers. The 4th electron is delocalised. Layers slide past each other → soft and slippery. Free electrons → conducts electricity.

walkthroughs.h2: Why metals are malleable and conductive
walkthroughs.body_html:
Metals are positive ions packed in regular layers, with a sea of delocalised electrons flowing around them.

Malleable: layers can slide over each other when hit — metal bends instead of shattering.

Conducts electricity: delocalised electrons drift through the lattice when a voltage is applied.

Conducts heat: those same electrons transfer kinetic energy quickly.

walkthroughs.h2: Why ionic compounds need to melt to conduct
walkthroughs.body_html:
Solid NaCl is a rigid lattice: Na⁺ and Cl⁻ locked in place. The ions can't move, so no current flows.

Melt it (or dissolve it in water) and the ions are free to move toward the opposite electrode → it conducts.

That's also why ionic compounds have high melting points: you have to break loads of strong ionic bonds before any ion can move.

options: It has delocalised electrons between its layers
The bonds are weak intermolecular forces
The layers of ions can slide over each other
They contain hollow tubes of atoms
They have very low melting points

numericals.q: In diamond, each carbon atom forms covalent bonds with how many neighbours?
numericals.hint: Think of a tetrahedral carbon — 4 bonds.

free_texts.q: What word describes electrons that are free to move through a metal or graphite? One word.
free_texts.hint: Not stuck in one place — opposite of 'localised'.
